claim: Phenotypic plasticity allows carcinoma cells to transiently acquire the quasi-mesenchymal features necessary to detach from the primary mass and proceed along the invasion-metastasis cascade.
source: Phenotypic plasticity allows carcinoma cells to transiently acquire the quasi-mesenchymal features necessary to detach from the primary mass and proceed along the invasion-metastasis cascade.
evidence: This is a general statement about phenotypic plasticity in cancer that draws from established scientific understanding of cancer biology.

claim: A broad spectrum of epigenetic mechanisms is likely to cause the epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) and mesenchymal-to-epithelial (MET) transitions necessary to allow local dissemination and distant metastasis.
source: A broad spectrum of epigenetic mechanisms is likely to cause the epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) and mesenchymal-to-epithelial (MET) transitions necessary to allow local dissemination and distant metastasis.
evidence: This statement involves speculative reasoning about the mechanisms underlying EMT/MET transitions.

claim: The differential expression of ESRP1 and other RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) downstream of the EMT master regulator ZEB1 alters the AS pattern of a broad spectrum of targets including CD44 and NUMB.
source: we here show that the differential expression of ESRP1 and other RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) downstream of the EMT master regulator ZEB1 alters the AS pattern of a broad spectrum of targets including CD44 and NUMB
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing differential expression patterns and alternative splicing changes.

claim: The CD44s and NUMB2/4 splicing isoforms promote local invasion and distant metastasis.
source: both the newly identified RBPs and the CD44s and NUMB2/4 splicing isoforms promote local invasion and distant metastasis
evidence: This is supported by functional validation studies including migration assays and in vivo metastasis experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The CD44s and NUMB2/4 splicing isoforms are associated with poor survival in colon cancer.
source: both the newly identified RBPs and the CD44s and NUMB2/4 splicing isoforms promote local invasion and distant metastasis and are associated with poor survival in colon cancer
evidence: This is supported by clinical validation studies using patient data from TCGA showing survival correlations.

claim: Colon cancer still represents one of the major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide.
source: Colon cancer still represents one of the major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the clinical significance of colon cancer.

claim: The adenoma-carcinoma sequence along which colon cancer progresses has served as a classic model to elucidate the underlying genetic alterations representative of virtually all of the hallmarks of cancers.
source: the adenoma-carcinoma sequence along which colon cancer progresses has served as a classic model to elucidate the underlying genetic alterations representative of virtually all of the hallmarks of cancers (Hanahan, 2022)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hanahan, 2022.

claim: The several steps of the invasion-metastasis cascade are not caused by genetic alterations but rather by transient morphological and gene expression changes of epigenetic nature.
source: the several steps of the invasion-metastasis cascade are not caused by genetic alterations but rather by transient morphological and gene expression changes of epigenetic nature (Bernards and Weinberg, 2002; Reiter et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bernards and Weinberg, 2002 and Reiter et al., 2018.

claim: EMT and MET likely represent the main mechanisms underlying local dissemination and distant metastasis.
source: epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and its reverse mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) likely represent the main mechanisms underlying local dissemination and distant metastasis (Thiery et al., 2009; Brabletz et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Thiery et al., 2009 and Brabletz et al., 2005.

claim: EMT is triggered at the invasive front of the primary colon carcinoma in cells earmarked by nuclear β-catenin and enhanced Wnt signaling.
source: EMT is triggered at the invasive front of the primary colon carcinoma in cells earmarked by nuclear β-catenin and enhanced Wnt signaling, as the result of their physical and paracrine interactions with the microenvironment (Fodde and Brabletz, 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fodde and Brabletz, 2007.

claim: EMT/MET should not be regarded as binary processes in view of the existence of metastable hybrid E/M states (partial EMT [pEMT]) endowed with phenotypic plasticity.
source: EMT/MET should not be regarded as binary processes in view of the existence of metastable hybrid E/M states (partial EMT [pEMT]) endowed with phenotypic plasticity and likely to underlie the reversible morphological and functional transitions necessary to successfully complete the invasion-metastasis cascade (Teeuwssen and Fodde, 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Teeuwssen and Fodde, 2019.

claim: The inclusion/exclusion of specific exons in mature mRNAs results in different protein isoforms with distinct biological functions.
source: The inclusion/exclusion of specific exons in mature mRNAs results in different protein isoforms with distinct biological functions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about alternative splicing mechanisms.

claim: AS occurs in 92–94% of human genes leading to enriched protein density.
source: AS occurs in 92–94% of human genes leading to enriched protein density (Wang et al., 2008; Blencowe, 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2008 and Blencowe, 2006.

claim: Multiple cancer-specific AS variants have been found to underlie progression and metastasis.
source: Multiple cancer-specific AS variants have been found to underlie progression and metastasis (Kahles et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kahles et al., 2018.

claim: AS has been suggested to play key roles in EMT/MET and phenotypic plasticity in cancer.
source: AS has been suggested to play key roles in EMT/MET (Roy Burman et al., 2021; Oltean and Bates, 2014) and phenotypic plasticity (Biamonti et al., 2019) in cancer
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Roy Burman et al., 2021, Oltean and Bates, 2014, and Biamonti et al., 2019.

claim: ESRP1 was reported to regulate the EMT from CD44v (variable) to CD44s (standard) isoforms in breast and lung cancer progression.
source: ESRP1 was reported to regulate the EMT from CD44v (variable) to CD44s (standard) isoforms in breast and lung cancer progression (Brown et al., 2011; Yae et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brown et al., 2011 and Yae et al., 2012.

claim: EpCAMlo cells feature highly invasive and metastatic capacities.
source: Accordingly, EpCAMlo cells feature highly invasive and metastatic capacities.
evidence: This is supported by previous characterization work cited in the manuscript (Sacchetti et al., 2021).

claim: ESRP1 was found to be downregulated both at the RNA and at the protein level in the quasi-mesenchymal subpopulation where ZEB1 expression is upregulated.
source: ESRP1 was found to be downregulated both at the RNA and at the protein level in the quasi-mesenchymal subpopulation where ZEB1 expression is upregulated (Figure 1A–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C including RT-qPCR and western blot analyses.

claim: ESRP1 overexpression in the HCT116 and SW480 cell lines resulted in the dramatic reduction of their EpCAMlo subpopulations and the expansion of the epithelial bulk (EpCAMhi).
source: ESRP1 overexpression in the HCT116 and SW480 cell lines resulted in the dramatic reduction of their EpCAMlo subpopulations and the expansion of the epithelial bulk (EpCAMhi), as shown by FACS analysis (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Apart from ESRP1, consistent differential expression in the quasi-mesenchymal subpopulation of both cell lines was observed for ESRP2, RBM47, MBNL3 (downregulated) and NOVA2, MBNL2 (upregulated).
source: Indeed, by taking advantage of the RBPDB database (Cook et al., 2011), we found that, apart from ESRP1, consistent differential expression in the quasi-mesenchymal subpopulation of both cell lines was observed for ESRP2, RBM47, MBNL3 (downregulated) and NOVA2, MBNL2 (upregulated)
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of the RBPDB database and comparison with experimental data.

claim: The RBP-coding genes QKI, RBM24, and MBNL2 (up in EpCAMlo), and ESRP1/2 and RBM47 (down in EpCAMlo) were found to be respectively up- and downregulated in the consensus molecular subtype 4 (CMS4) of colon cancers.
source: the RBP-coding genes QKI, RBM24, and MBNL2 (up in EpCAMlo), and ESRP1/2 and RBM47 (down in EpCAMlo) were found to be respectively up- and downregulated in the consensus molecular subtype 4 (CMS4) of colon cancers, responsible for ~25% of the cases and earmarked by poor prognosis and a pronounced mesenchymal component (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D; Guinney et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of TCGA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and cited work by Guinney et al., 2015.

claim: A total of 32 common skipped exons events in 20 genes were identified between EpCAMlo colon (both cell lines) and ESRP1 KD H358 lung cancer cells.
source: A total of 32 common skipped exons events in 20 genes were identified between EpCAMlo colon (both cell lines) and ESRP1 KD H358 lung cancer cells (Yang et al., 2016; Figure 2A)
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative analysis of RNAseq data shown in Figure 2A and cited work by Yang et al., 2016.

claim: Four EMT-related genes (CTNND1, LSR, SLK, and TCF7L2) were common to all RBP KD studies analyzed.
source: Notably, four EMT-related genes (CTNND1 Hernández-Martínez et al., 2019, LSR Shimada et al., 2021, SLK Conway et al., 2017, and TCF7L2 Karve et al., 2020) were common to all RBP KD studies analyzed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and multiple citations.

claim: CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms were preferentially expressed in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, in contrast with the increased CD44v and NUMB1/3 levels in EpCAMhi cells.
source: RT-qPCR and western analyses validated these in silico data: CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms were preferentially expressed in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, in contrast with the increased CD44v and NUMB1/3 levels in EpCAMhi cells (Figure 2C–D)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: ESRP1 knockdown resulted in the upregulation of the CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms at the mRNA and protein level in both cell lines.
source: The dox-inducible shRNA vector used for the KD studies reduces ESRP1 expression by 5- to 10-fold (Figure 1D–E) and resulted in the upregulation of the CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms at the mRNA and protein level in both cell lines (Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: ESRP1 overexpression led to an increase in the CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 isoforms.
source: Likewise, ESRP1 overexpression led to an increase in the CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 isoforms, found in association with the bulk of epithelial colon cancer cells (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Overexpression of the CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms resulted in a significant increase in migratory capacity comparable to that of EpCAMlo cells.
source: A significant increase in migratory capacity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–B), comparable to that of EpCAMlo cells sorted from the parental lines, was observed in SW480 and HCT116 upon overexpression of the CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–B)
evidence: This claim is supported by migration assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Overexpression of CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 did not affect migratory properties.
source: In contrast, overexpression of CD44v6 and NUMB1/3, normally prevalent in the epithelial bulk (EpCAMhi) of both cell lines, did not affect their migratory properties (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–B)
evidence: This claim is supported by migration assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Overexpression of CD44s and NUMB2/4 results in the significant upregulation of the EMT transcription factors ZEB1, accompanied by the up- and downregulation of mesenchymal and epithelial markers such as VIM (vimentin), CDH1 (E-cadherin), and EpCAM.
source: In agreement with the migration assays, overexpression of CD44s and NUMB2/4 results in the significant upregulation of the EMT transcription factors (EMT-TFs) ZEB1, accompanied by the up- and downregulation regulation of mesenchymal and epithelial markers such as VIM (vimentin), CDH1 (E-cadherin), and EpCAM, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Expression of ESRP1 was decreased in CD44s- and NUMB2/4-OE cells, in confirmation of the self-enforcing feedback loop that characterize its interaction with ZEB1 and EMT activation.
source: Of note, expression of ESRP1, the main upstream splicing regulator of both CD44 and NUMB, was also decreased in CD44s- and NUMB2/4-OE cells, in confirmation of the self-enforcing feedback loop that characterize its interaction with ZEB1 and EMT activation (Preca et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations and a citation to Preca et al., 2015.

claim: Established Notch target genes were up- (HES1, HEY1) and downregulated (ID2) upon overexpression of NUMB2/4.
source: In agreement with the well-established regulation of Notch signaling by NUMB isoforms (Pece et al., 2011), established Notch target genes and were accordingly up- (HES1, HEY1) and downregulated (ID2) upon overexpression of NUMB2/4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D and a citation to Pece et al., 2011.

claim: CD44s overexpression led to a dramatic increase of the EpCAMlo subpopulation at the expenses of EpCAMhi cells.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, CD44s overexpression led to a dramatic increase of the EpCAMlo subpopulation at the expenses of EpCAMhi cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: CD44v6 overexpression resulted in the enlargement of the EpCAMhi gate and the corresponding decrease of EpCAMlo cells.
source: The opposite effect was observed with CD44v6, that is, the enlargement of the EpCAMhi gate and the corresponding decrease of EpCAMlo cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the FACS analysis results described in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Ectopic expression of NUMB2/4 significantly increased the relative proportion of EpCAMlo cells while reducing the size of the EpCAMhi subpopulation.
source: As for NUMB, ectopic expression of NUMB2/4 significantly increased the relative proportion of EpCAMlo cells while reducing the size of the EpCAMhi subpopulation, while the opposite was observed with NUMB1/3 (Figure 4B–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figures 4B-C.

claim: CD44s overexpression negatively affected overall proliferation rates in both cell lines, whereas the opposite was observed upon CD44v6 expression.
source: In agreement with the RTqPCR analysis of EMT markers, CD44s overexpression negatively affected overall proliferation rates in both cell lines, whereas the opposite was observed upon CD44v6 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–B)
evidence: This claim is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: NUMB1/3 expression positively affected proliferation rates in HCT116 and SW480, whereas the NUMB2/4 isoforms exert the opposite effects.
source: Likewise, NUMB1/3 expression positively affected proliferation rates in HCT116 and SW480, whereas the NUMB2/4 isoforms exert the opposite effects.
evidence: This claim is supported by proliferation assay data referenced in the text.

claim: Overexpression of both NUMB2/4 and CD44s isoforms significantly increased the multiplicity of liver metastases, whereas CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 did not differ from the parental controls.
source: In agreement with the in vitro results, overexpression of both NUMB2/4 and CD44s isoforms significantly increased the multiplicity of liver metastases, whereas CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 did not differ from the parental controls (Figure 4D–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo spleen transplantation data shown in Figures 4D-E.

claim: EMT was the only pathway upregulated in CD44s vs. CD44v6 in both cell lines.
source: Among the significantly altered pathways (normalized enrichment score [NES] >1, pval <0.05), EMT was the only one upregulated in CD44s vs. CD44v6 in both cell lines (Figure 5C–D)
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figures 5C-D.

claim: ZEB1hi tumors have an overall decreased survival probability (p=0.045).
source: Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that ZEB1hi tumors have an overall decreased survival probability (p=0.045) (Figure 6B)
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis shown in Figure 6B using TCGA data.

claim: While no significant differences were observed based on the expression level of the whole CD44 and NUMB genes, significant differences were found for their specific isoforms.
source: Notably, while no significant differences were observed based on the expression level of the whole CD44 and NUMB genes, significant differences were found for their specific isoforms (Figure 6C)
evidence: This claim is supported by expression analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Analysis of the specific isoforms expression across the different CMS revealed elevated CD44s and NUMB2/4 expression in the CMS4 subtype.
source: Analysis of the specific isoforms expression across the different CMS (Guinney et al., 2015) revealed elevated CD44s and NUMB2/4 expression in the CMS4 subtype, known to be enriched in mesenchymal lineages in tumor and TME cells, and strongly associated with poor survival and the greatest propensity to form distant metastases (Figure 6D)
evidence: This claim is supported by expression analysis shown in Figure 6D and citation to Guinney et al., 2015.

claim: The majority of the ZEB1hi group was composed of the CMS4 subtype (72%), while the ZEB1lo group was mainly contributed by CMS2 (49%) and CMS3 tumors (31%), with few CMS4 tumors (1%).
source: Likewise, the majority of the ZEB1hi group was composed of the CMS4 subtype (72%), while the ZEB1lo group was mainly contributed by CMS2 (49%) and CMS3 tumors (31%), with few CMS4 tumors (1%) (Figure 6E)
evidence: This claim is supported by compositional analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms showed overall similar correlating hallmarks and pathways.
source: The CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms showed overall similar correlating hallmarks and pathways.
evidence: This claim is based on pathway correlation analysis described in the text.

claim: Most invasion/metastasis-relevant hallmarks (e.g. EMT, angiogenesis, apical junctions) showed a positive correlation with CD44s and NUMB2/4, though not with CD44v6 and NUMB1/3.
source: Here, most invasion/metastasis-relevant hallmarks (e.g. EMT, angiogenesis, apical junctions) showed a positive correlation with CD44s and NUMB2/4, though not with CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 (Figure 7B)
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway correlation analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Expression of the EpCAMlo-specific isoforms (CD44s and NUMB2/4) is elevated in CMS4 tumors.
source: Expression of the EpCAMlo-specific isoforms (CD44s and NUMB2/4) is elevated in CMS4 tumors overall survival.
evidence: This claim is supported by expression analysis of TCGA data stratified by CMS classification.

claim: Both NUMB2/4 and CD44s isoforms appear to be upregulated in the OV90 and SKOV6 cell lines.
source: As shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1, both NUMB2/4 and CD44s isoforms appear to be upregulated in the OV90 and SKOV6 cell lines, as also validated by RT-qPCR.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ESRP1/2 genes were found among the top downregulated RBP-coding genes in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, as part of a self-enforcing feedback loop with the EMT-TF ZEB1.
source: The ESRP1/2 genes (Warzecha et al., 2009), the 'splicing masterminds' of EMT (Tavanez and Valcárcel, 2010; Warzecha et al., 2010), were found among the top downregulated RBP-coding genes in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, as part of a self-enforcing feedback loop with the EMT-TF ZEB1 (Preca et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and multiple citations.

claim: ZEB1 upregulation in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells is invariably accompanied by ESRP1/2 downregulation.
source: Accordingly, ZEB1 upregulation in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells is invariably accompanied by ESRP1/2 downregulation
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations described in the manuscript.

claim: ZEB1hi/ESRP1lo colon cancers, predominantly belonging to the mesenchymal CMS4 subgroup, have a significantly worse survival outcome when compared with ZEB1lo/ESRP1hi patients.
source: and ZEB1hi/ESRP1lo colon cancers, predominantly belonging to the mesenchymal CMS4 subgroup, have a significantly worse survival outcome when compared with ZEB1lo/ESRP1hi patients
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis of TCGA patient data.

claim: The same QKI, RBM24, and MBNL2 genes were found to have increased expression in CMS4 tumors, known for their pronounced mesenchymal composition and poor prognosis.
source: Accordingly, in patient-derived colon cancers stratified according to their consensus molecular signature, the same QKI, RBM24, and MBNL2 genes were found to have increased expression in CMS4 tumors, known for their pronounced mesenchymal composition and poor prognosis (Guinney et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of patient data and citation to Guinney et al., 2015.

claim: The EpCAMlo cells do represent bona fide quasi-mesenchymal colon cancer cells, enriched among CMS4 cases, and likely responsible for their poor prognosis.
source: As shown in our previous study (Sacchetti et al., 2021), the EpCAMlo cells do represent bona fide quasi-mesenchymal colon cancer cells, enriched among CMS4 cases, and likely responsible for their poor prognosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by Sacchetti et al., 2021.

claim: The observed upregulation of RBPs such as quaking (QKI) is caused by the presence in its 3'UTR of target sequences of the miR-200 family of microRNAs.
source: The observed upregulation of RBPs such as quaking (QKI) is caused by the presence in its 3'UTR of target sequences of the miR-200 family of microRNAs (Pillman et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pillman et al., 2018 and Kim et al., 2019.

claim: The significantly reduced levels of all five miR-200 members in EpCAMlo cells underlie the coordinated upregulation of both ZEB1 and QKI.
source: Accordingly, the significantly reduced levels of all five miR-200 members in EpCAMlo cells (Sacchetti et al., 2021) underly the coordinated upregulation of both ZEB1 and QKI.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from previous data cited from Sacchetti et al., 2021.

claim: The here observed RBM47 downregulation in CMS4 colon cancers is in agreement with a previous report on its decreased protein expression during EMT in association with metastasis in a cohort of primary CRCs.
source: The here observed RBM47 downregulation in CMS4 colon cancers is in agreement with a previous report on its decreased protein expression during EMT in association with metastasis in a cohort of primary CRCs (Rokavec et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rokavec et al., 2017.

claim: The increased expression of other RBP-coding genes such as RBM24 and MBNL2 (muscleblind-like 2) in CMS4 tumors and in EpCAMlo cells is in sharp contradiction with their alleged tumor suppressing roles in colon and other cancers.
source: On the other hand, the increased expression of other RBP-coding genes such as RBM24 and MBNL2 (muscleblind-like 2) in CMS4 tumors and in EpCAMlo cells is in sharp contradiction with their alleged tumor suppressing roles in colon and other cancers (Xia et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of the current findings with previous literature cited.

claim: MBNL2 regulates cancer migration and invasion through PI3K/AKT-mediated EMT.
source: Of note, MBNL2 regulates cancer migration and invasion through PI3K/AKT-mediated EMT (Lin et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2021.

claim: Overexpression of MBNL2 in breast and cancer cell lines inhibits their metastatic potential.
source: and its overexpression in breast and cancer cell lines inhibits their metastatic potential (Zhang et al., 2019b)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2019b.

claim: MBNL3 is downregulated in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, similar to what reported in prostate cancer.
source: In contrast to MBNL2, MBNL3, a distinct member of the muscleblind family, is downregulated in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, similar to what reported in prostate cancer by Lu et al., 2015.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to Lu et al., 2015.

claim: NOVA2 was upregulated in the quasi-mesenchymal cells from both cell lines, possibly as the result of the differential expression of miR-7-5p.
source: NOVA2, a member of the Nova family of neuron-specific RBPs, was also upregulated in the quasi-mesenchymal cells from both cell lines, possibly as the result of the differential expression of miR-7-5p (Xiao, 2019), as previously shown in non-small cell lung (Xiao, 2019) and prostate (Lu et al., 2015) cancer.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Xiao, 2019 and Lu et al., 2015.

claim: The top four AS targets common to all of the RBPs (CTNND1, LSR, SLK, and TCF7L2) are known regulators and effectors of EMT.
source: By following this admittedly imperfect approach, the top four AS targets common to all of the above-mentioned RBPs notwithstanding their up- or downregulation in EpCAMlo colon cancer cells, that is, CTNND1 (δ- or p120-catenin), LSR (lipolysis stimulated lipoprotein receptor), SLK (STE20-like kinase), and TCF7L2 (transcription factor 7-like 2, or TCF4) are known regulators and effectors of EMT (Hernández-Martínez et al., 2019; Shimada et al., 2021; Conway et al., 2017; Karve et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms appear to be specifically expressed in quasi-mesenchymal colon cancer cells both from the immortalized cell lines and from patient-derived tumors, with a striking enrichment in the CMS4 subgroup of colon cancer patients.
source: The CD44s and NUMB2/4 isoforms appear to be specifically expressed in quasi-mesenchymal colon cancer cells both from the immortalized cell lines and from patient-derived tumors, with a striking enrichment in the CMS4 subgroup of colon cancer patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell lines and patient tumor analysis.

claim: The CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 isoforms are preferentially expressed in the epithelial bulk of the tumor.
source: In contrast, the CD44v6 and NUMB1/3 isoforms are preferentially expressed in the epithelial bulk of the tumor.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell lines and patient tumor analysis.

claim: CD44v6 and other 'variable' CD44 isoforms (CD44v4-10) earmark Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells (ISCs), that is, the cells of origin of intestinal tumors, and accordingly promote adenoma formation in vivo.
source: CD44v6 and other 'variable' CD44 isoforms (CD44v4-10) earmark Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells (ISCs), that is, the cells of origin of intestinal tumors, and accordingly promote adenoma formation in vivo (Zeilstra et al., 2008; Zeilstra et al., 2014; Misra et al., 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zeilstra et al., 2008, Zeilstra et al., 2014, and Misra et al., 2009.

claim: The CD44v6 isoform is required for c-MET activation by hepatocyte growth factor (HGF, or scatter factor).
source: The CD44v6 isoform is required for c-MET activation by hepatocyte growth factor (HGF, or scatter factor) (Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Orian-Rousseau et al., 2002.

claim: CD44v6 but not CD44s binds to cMET in response to HGF stimulation.
source: Our own immunoprecipitation studies confirmed that CD44v6 but not CD44s binds to cMET in response to HGF stimulation (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by unpublished experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: Both CD44 isoforms are essential for the completion of the invasion-metastasis cascade.
source: From this perspective, both CD44 isoforms are essential for the completion of the invasion-metastasis cascade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional roles of the different isoforms described in the manuscript.

claim: The functional relevance of the CD44s isoforms has been highlighted in malignancies other than colon cancer, namely in prostate and breast cancer where it activates, among others, PDGFRβ/Stat3 and Akt signaling to promote EMT and CSC traits.
source: The functional relevance of the CD44s isoforms has been highlighted in malignancies other than colon cancer, namely in prostate (Lu et al., 2015) and breast cancer where it activates, among others, PDGFRβ/Stat3 and Akt signaling to promote EMT and CSC traits (Brown et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2019a)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2015, Brown et al., 2011, and Zhang et al., 2019a.

claim: Among the DEGs identified upon CD44s ectopic expression which correlate with ZEB1hi/ESRP1lo (and CMS4) colon cancers, the SPARC gene, a pEMT marker in the EpCAMhi/lo state transitions, was found.
source: Of note, among the DEGs identified upon CD44s ectopic expression which correlate with ZEB1hi/ESRP1lo (and CMS4) colon cancers, the SPARC gene, a pEMT marker in the EpCAMhi/lo state transitions (Sacchetti et al., 2021), was found.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq analysis and citation to Sacchetti et al., 2021.

claim: Expression of NUMB2/4 isoforms both in cells lines and in patient-derived colon tumors is associated with signaling pathways and GO categories largely overlapping with those linked to CD44s.
source: Expression of NUMB2/4 isoforms both in cells lines and in patient-derived colon tumors is associated with signaling pathways and GO categories largely overlapping with those linked to CD44s (and CD44v6 with NUMB1/3), possibly suggesting synergism between AS at these genes.
evidence: This claim is based on pathway analysis of RNAseq data and suggests a speculative interpretation.

claim: NUMB inhibits EMT by suppressing the Notch signaling pathway.
source: NUMB inhibits EMT by suppressing the Notch signaling pathway.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NUMB function.

claim: Downregulation of NUMB can induce an EMT phenotype in isoform-specific fashion.
source: As such, downregulation of NUMB can induce an EMT phenotype in isoform-specific fashion.
evidence: This is based on inference from the experimental results presented.

claim: Analysis of colon cancer cells individually overexpressing each of the four isoforms revealed an increased basal Notch signaling in NUMB2 and -4, as shown by the expression of the 'universal' targets HES1 and HEY1.
source: Analysis of colon cancer cells individually overexpressing each of the four isoforms revealed an increased basal Notch signaling in NUMB2 and -4, as shown by the expression of the 'universal' targets HES1 and HEY1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on Notch target gene expression.

claim: Ectopic expression of NUMB1/3 resulted in increased transcriptional levels of the more atypical Notch signaling target ID2.
source: Instead, ectopic expression of NUMB1/3 resulted in increased transcriptional levels of the more atypical Notch signaling target ID2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on Notch target gene expression.

claim: AS substantially contributes to the epigenetic mechanisms that underlie EMT/MET in cancer metastasis.
source: Overall, it appears that AS substantially contributes to the epigenetic mechanisms that underlie EMT/MET in cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: The systematic elucidation of the RBPs and AS targets which underlie phenotypic plasticity in different types of cancer will provide novel tumor-specific targets for therapeutic intervention based on small molecule inhibitors and even RNA vaccination.
source: Finally, the systematic elucidation of the RBPs and AS targets which underlie phenotypic plasticity in different types of cancer will provide novel tumor-specific targets for therapeutic intervention based on small molecule inhibitors and even RNA vaccination.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future therapeutic applications.
